main_body: two-story timber and stone building with hipped tile roof
top_band: brown tiled roof slope from row 1 to row 42
evidence: Rows 1-42 show the full foreshortened hipped roof slope (top band), followed by a dark eave line at row 43 and cast eave shadow across rows 44-47 above the two-story south wall face (rows 44-106) with recessed windows and door.

style.evidence: The candidate is a 4-color reduction of a Beodeul-style house: the entire image uses only 4 tones (cream, mid-brown, dark brown, near-black). The upper plaster wall panels are completely flat cream fills (12x16+ px with zero speckle, unlike the speckled plaster on the reference), the windows and sign are solid dark silhouettes, and the roof tiles and stones lack the multi-step per-tile highlights and shading of the reference.
